reason: The cited evidence confirms that Ti–Zn intermetallics influence corrosion through barrier or galvanic effects depending on distribution (E1, E2) and that fine intermetallics promote protective films (E3). However, none of the passages provide evidence for Mg segregation at defects or grain boundaries, nor for stepwise annealing inducing such segregation, leaving the core mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: Mg segregation at defect clusters and grain boundaries can be induced by stepwise annealing
Mg-rich zones serve as preferential nucleation sites for intermetallic phases
Fine, coherent intermetallic distribution promotes protective surface films and corrosion/oxidation resistance
Coarse or continuous intermetallic networks degrade performance via galvanic interactions and phase coarsening
Ti–Zn intermetallics can act as corrosion barriers or cathodic sites depending on distribution and morphology
